fact: Water expands by about 9% when it freezes, which is why ice floats on liquid water.
Diamonds and the graphite in pencils are both made of pure carbon, just arranged differently.
A single lightning bolt is roughly five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Sound cannot travel through the vacuum of space because there is no medium to carry the vibrations.
Properly sealed honey can remain edible for thousands of years thanks to its low moisture and acidity.
Glass is technically an amorphous solid, not a crystalline one, because its molecules are arranged irregularly.
A day on Venus (about 243 Earth days) is longer than its year (about 225 Earth days).
Neutron stars are so dense that a sugar-cube-sized piece of one would weigh roughly a billion tons.
Because there is no wind or water on the Moon, the footprints left by Apollo astronauts could last for millions of years.
Saturn's moon Titan has lakes and rivers made of liquid methane and ethane instead of water.
The Sun makes up about 99.8% of the total mass of our entire solar system.
About one million Earths could fit inside the volume of the Sun.
Octopuses have three hearts and blue blood, because their blood uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen.
A group of flamingos is called a 'flamboyance'.
Elephants are among the few animals known to recognize themselves in a mirror, a sign of self-awareness.
Sea otters often hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart in the water.
A shrimp's heart is located in its head.
Some turtles can absorb oxygen through their cloaca, letting them stay underwater for long stretches during hibernation.
The term computer 'bug' traces back to an actual moth found in a Harvard Mark II relay in 1947.
The QWERTY keyboard layout was originally designed to reduce jamming in mechanical typewriters, not to maximize typing speed.
The vast majority of the world's money exists only as digital records rather than physical cash or coins.
IBM's first 1GB hard disk drive, announced in 1980, weighed about 550 pounds (250 kg).
'Wi-Fi' is not actually an acronym for 'Wireless Fidelity' — it's simply a brand name.
One of the first webcams was built at Cambridge University just to monitor how full a coffee pot was.
Teaching at Oxford University began around 1096, making it older than the Aztec Empire.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.
The Great Fire of London in 1666 destroyed most of the city but is officially recorded as causing only a handful of deaths.
Napoleon Bonaparte was about 5'7" (170 cm) tall, roughly average height for a Frenchman of his era.
The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896, the shortest recorded war in history, lasted under 40 minutes.
Ancient Romans reportedly used urine, for its ammonia content, as an ingredient in cleaning products and mouth rinses.
Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country in the world.
Africa is the only continent that lies in all four hemispheres: northern, southern, eastern, and western.
Canada is estimated to have more lakes than the rest of the world combined.
The Sahara Desert was a green, fertile landscape with lakes and grassland thousands of years ago.
Vatican City is the smallest sovereign country in the world by both area and population.
Mount Everest grows a few millimeters taller each year due to ongoing tectonic plate movement.
The human body contains enough iron, mostly in the blood, to make a small nail.
Pound for pound, human bone is about as strong as steel but far lighter.
The brain uses roughly 20% of the body's total energy despite making up only about 2% of body weight.
Stomach acid is strong enough to damage some metals, but the stomach lining regenerates constantly to protect itself.
Humans shed roughly 30,000 to 40,000 dead skin cells every hour.
An average adult heart beats about 100,000 times per day.
Certain species of bamboo can grow up to 91 cm (36 inches) in a single day.
Bananas are botanically classified as berries, while strawberries technically are not.
Lightning can and often does strike the same location more than once, contrary to the popular saying.
Groves of aspen trees can share a single connected root system, making them technically one organism.
Rainforests cover only about 6% of Earth's land but are home to more than half of its plant and animal species.
A Venus flytrap counts how many times an insect touches its trigger hairs before the trap snaps shut.
The 'Mandela Effect' describes when large groups of people confidently share the same false memory.
Multitasking usually lowers productivity because the brain is switching between tasks rather than truly doing them at once.
People tend to remember the first and last items on a list best, a pattern known as the serial position effect.
Even a forced smile can slightly improve mood, a phenomenon linked to the facial feedback hypothesis.
Some cognitive research estimates the average person has thousands of distinct thoughts over the course of a day.
Most people experience déjà vu at some point, though scientists still debate its exact cause.
Honeybees can learn to recognize individual human faces using a process similar to how people do.
A single strand of spaghetti has its own name in Italian: 'spaghetto'.
There are more possible unique chess games than there are atoms in the observable universe.
The world's oldest known written recipe is for beer, dating back roughly 5,000 years to ancient Sumer.
Octopuses and some other cephalopods can change both the color and texture of their skin almost instantly.
The shortest commercial flight in the world, between two Scottish islands, can take under two minutes.
